text.title: Accessibility Evaluation Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 antipatterns observed when applying accessibility-evaluation; each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: Agent inserts alt="Description" placeholders that satisfy automated checks but fail SC 1.1.1 for context-specific images.
antipattern.root-cause: Placeholder passes attribute-present check; the alt-equivalent-information criterion is harder to test. Agent generating alt="Description" placeholders that pass automated checks but fail SC 1.1.1 for decorative or context-specific images. Placeholder alt text passes the "attribute present" check but fails the "alternative text conveys equivalent information" criterion. Require the agent to cite the source content the alt is derived from.
antipattern.fix: Require the agent to cite the source content the alt text is derived from; reject placeholders.

antipattern.symptom: Contrast fix in light mode silently creates a new violation in dark mode.
antipattern.root-cause: Token-layer edits propagate across modes; CI runs only light mode. Agent fixing contrast by editing CSS variables without checking dark-mode token consistency. Token-layer edits propagate to all modes. A contrast fix in light mode can create a new violation in dark mode. Require diffs with both modes regenerated.
antipattern.fix: Regenerate both modes; CI compares contrast in both before approval.

antipattern.symptom: Agent mass-adds aria-label to buttons that already have visible text labels with different wording — creates SC 2.5.3 violation.
antipattern.root-cause: Auto-fix script does not check accessible-name vs visible-text consistency. Agent mass-adding aria-label to elements that already have visible text labels. Adding aria-label to an element with visible text creates a SC 2.5.3 (Label in Name) violation if the label text differs. Lint for accessible-name vs visible-text mismatch before applying.
antipattern.fix: Lint accessible-name vs visible-text mismatch before applying any aria-label.

antipattern.symptom: Stakeholder claims AA conformance based on a Stage-1 axe-clean report.
antipattern.root-cause: Tools miss 60-70% of issues; stages 3+4 skipped.
antipattern.fix: Block conformance claim unless Stages 1-5 all signed off with evidence.

antipattern.symptom: Agent closing findings as "won't fix" without a human accessibility lead sign-off with documented rationale.
antipattern.root-cause: Suppressed findings without rationale create phantom compliance. Legal and procurement reviewers will ask for documented risk acceptance; agents cannot provide it.
antipattern.fix: Only a named human accessibility lead may close a finding as won't-fix, and the closure carries a written risk-acceptance rationale.

antipattern.symptom: Scanning logged-out fallback pages instead of authenticated application states.
antipattern.root-cause: Authenticated pages have additional dynamic content, modals, and forms not visible to unauthenticated scans. Clean reports from unauthenticated pages are false negatives.
antipattern.fix: Scan with an authenticated session (storage state or test account) and list the authenticated routes covered in the report scope.
